title: dynamic-econ-configurator-tenant-warmstart-hints-and-defaults
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: tenants frequently land on conservative batching/caching defaults that underutilize available KV-cache or over-quantize models to save cost, producing avoidable latency or quality regressions. We need an automated, tenant-aware generator that combines short traffic fingerprints, unit-economics targets, and model compatibility to produce pragmatic defaults: batch shapes, prefill hints, cache TTLs, and a ranked set of quantization profiles.

What this PR does: introduces the Dynamic Econ Configurator service and a small CLI to dry-run tenant-level defaults. The configurator ingests a short traffic fingerprint (percentiles for request size, seq lengths, warm/cold start ratio), a tenant SLO/cost target, and model metadata, then emits a candidate defaults bundle and confidence score. It also wires in telemetry and a dry-run flow integrated into the onboarding pipeline.

High-level design: the service contains three components: (1) fingerprint collector (lightweight sampling hook in runtime/prefill) that produces anonymized histograms, (2) decision core that maps fingerprints to templates using a compact rule-set + simple regression to estimate per-token cost and tail latency, (3) profile composer that emits batching, cache, and quantization presets as a single bundle. The decision core prefers smallest-risk changes first (cache TTL and prefill thresholds) and only suggests quantization when unit-econ delta exceeds threshold and quality risk score is low.

Checklist (what I changed):
- [x] new service: services/econ-configurator with HTTP API and proto definitions
- [x] fingerprint collector hook in runtime/prefill (sampling + anonymization)
- [x] CLI: ./bin/econctl dry-run --tenant <id> --fingerprint <path>
- [x] telemetry: metrics for suggestions, confidence, and estimated unit-econ impact
- [x] unit and integration tests (decision core offline tests + end-to-end dry-run)
- [x] docs: docs/guide/econ-configurator.md with usage and safety notes

Backward compatibility & safety: output is opt-in; runtime treats emitted bundles as suggestions unless applied via the Console or the econctl apply command. All suggestions include a safe rollback plan and an automatic A/B canary policy when applied. No runtime behavior is changed by default.

How we tested: unit tests cover the rule-set edgecases; an end-to-end dry-run was executed on a synthetic tenant trace (see tests/fixtures/synthetic-tenant-1.json) and compared against baseline defaults. Perf-smoke runs showed median latency within 1% and cost estimate improvement ~14% in the synthetic run. Integration tests ran in CI and passed after one flake rerun.

Next steps: hook configurator into onboarding pipeline to suggest initial defaults and expose an opt-in batch for gradual rollout (ENG-3499). Longer-term: replace the regression estimator with a lightweight trained model once we have 10k tenant fingerprints.

release_notes:
- New: Dynamic Econ Configurator service to generate tenant-level batching/caching/quantization suggestions (opt-in)
- New: econctl dry-run to preview suggested bundles
- Metrics: econ.suggestions.count, econ.suggestion.confidence, econ.estimated.unit_econ_delta
- Safety: suggestions are non-destructive by default and include rollback plans
